# CHRONIC PROSTATITIS / CHRONIC PELVIC PAIN SYNDROME
Chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS) is a clinical syndrome in males defined by pain or discomfort in the pelvic region, often accompanied by urologic symptoms or sexual dysfunction. Despite the use of the term "prostatitis," it is unclear to what degree the prostate is the source of symptoms.
Research guidelines define chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS) as chronic pelvic pain for at least three of the preceding six months in the absence of other identifiable causes, often associated with urinary symptoms and/or sexual dysfunction.

This syndrome presents with intermittent perineal and/or low back pain, obstructive voiding symptoms, relatively normal examination, and negative urine cultures. In patients who have a negative urine culture and features consistent with CP/CPPS, antimicrobial therapy is not indicated.
Consult urology for non-antimicrobial therapy recommendations (e.g. alpha-adrenergic antagonists, anti-inflammatory medications) to reduce symptoms.

## Anti-inflammatory treatment

Ibuprofen 400 mg PO q8h for 1 to 3 weeks
